inputs.root_cause: ORA-STACK-001's 14 obligations all cited an identical generic '3-shared-root-attribute-test' citation despite model/stack.py and codec/stack_xml.py already implementing and, for most rule_texts, already directly testing the specific behavior each obligation names -- the same 'started but not finished' audit pattern found repeatedly this session (XLIFF-SEG-001, ORA-RESOLUTION-001/ISOLATION-001, ORA-BASELINEASSET-001). Investigated the UBL/XLIFF preservation-mode thread's natural follow-up candidates (ORA-MASK-001, ORA-COMPOSITE-001) first but found both require inventing spec content (composite-op inventory, mask element shape) not backed by any committed SAL fact -- declined per this session's anti-fabrication discipline and pivoted to this citation audit instead.
inputs.obligation_targeted: SAL-ORA-OBL-047E5523BB0D85D5, SAL-ORA-OBL-1BCC64FF1DFE8AE5, SAL-ORA-OBL-23D0207100C46AD9, SAL-ORA-OBL-329D93743655752D, SAL-ORA-OBL-6078C4F67F33C8E4, SAL-ORA-OBL-9007B671A8FCFF7D, SAL-ORA-OBL-930CACD129A5CC40, SAL-ORA-OBL-BFEC595E47C33BE7, SAL-ORA-OBL-D76D780D4D9DA699, SAL-ORA-OBL-F6424763BCEC7266, SAL-ORA-OBL-4EC8C1CC747F7FC6
inputs.acceptance_evidence: tests/python/ora/test_obligation_stack_and_document.py (existing tests, individually cited per obligation) plus 2 new tests for <text>-via-XML parsing

execution_steps: 1. Pulled the rule_text for each of ORA-STACK-001's 14 obligations from the obligation register (not just the evidence file) to see what each ACTUALLY requires, since the shared generic citation gave no per-obligation signal.

2. Read model/stack.py and codec/stack_xml.py in full, then read test_obligation_stack_and_document.py in full and mapped each of the 14 distinct rule_texts to the specific existing test(s) that already prove it directly -- most were already fully proven by name-matched tests (opacity range, required src, visibility enum, xres/yres pairing, x/y signed defaults, root w/h/version).

3. Found two rule_texts under ORA-STACK-001 are cross-capability duplicates of already-closed or already-investigated obligations elsewhere: SAL-ORA-OBL-BFEC595E47C33BE7's rule_text ('a non-root stack is isolated when isolation is isolate, opacity is below one, or composite-op differs from svg:src-over') is word-for-word identical to ORA-ISOLATION-001's already-implemented SAL-ORA-OBL-97CE271E3DD6D883 -- closed by citation, extended ORA-RESOLUTION-ISOLATION-SELECTOR-PROOF's covered-obligations list. SAL-ORA-OBL-930CACD129A5CC40's composite-op rule_text is identical to ORA-COMPOSITE-001's SAL-ORA-OBL-4EC8C1CC747F7FC6 (found while investigating ORA-COMPOSITE-001 first, before pivoting to this audit).

4. For the composite-op obligation (930CACD129A5CC40 and its duplicate 4EC8C1CC747F7FC6): confirmed via test_composite_op_defaults_to_src_over and test_composite_op_is_preserved_verbatim that the default value and open-vocabulary preservation ARE proven, but no registry anywhere in the package maps a composite-op string to 'a documented blend function combined with a Porter-Duff compositing operator' -- a confirmed, real gap. Checked shared/sal-facts/ora.yaml for the actual OpenRaster composite-op inventory before considering building a registry: the only committed fact is the generic default-plus-general-claim sentence, not an enumerated operation list. Declined to invent the list from memory (would risk fabricating spec content) and corrected both obligations to accurate `partial` (was `missing` for 4EC8C1CC747F7FC6, which incorrectly implied nothing was proven) with a precise missing_behavior naming exactly what remains and why it was not attempted.

5. Found one genuine, narrow, buildable test gap: 'A stack element contains nested stack, layer, or text elements' (SAL-ORA-OBL-329D93743655752D) was only proven for stack+layer nesting; the <text> child kind was implemented in codec/stack_xml.py's _Walker.child (its own error message quotes this obligation's rule text verbatim) but never exercised through the actual XML parser in any test -- only via direct OraText(...) construction in test_obligation_layer_and_group_editing.py, bypassing the parser entirely.

6. Added two new tests to test_obligation_stack_and_document.py: test_a_text_element_parses_as_a_stack_child (text with src) and test_a_text_element_without_src_parses_with_src_none (text's src is optional, unlike layer's). Ran ruff (clean) and the file's full suite (51 passed) before citing.
7. Ran every candidate test directly (not just the two new ones) before citing any of them, confirming each obligation's specific claim.

8. Promoted 8 of 14 ORA-STACK-001 obligations to fully implemented with specific (not shared) source_symbols and test selectors, closed 1 as a cross-capability duplicate citation, corrected 1 (plus its ORA-COMPOSITE-001 duplicate) to accurate narrowed partial. Left the remaining 4 (baseline-support-levels goal statement, interop-and-no-destructive-pixel-ops goal statement, root-versus-non-root modeling constraint, UTF-8-encoding-specific test coverage) unaudited rather than force-promoted -- each is either a broad policy statement not cleanly reducible to one test, or has a real but narrower remaining test gap not fully investigated this tick.

9. Hit the known contract_reconciler.py pitfall twice: DEFAULT_COMPOSITE_OP and VISIBILITY_VALUES are module-level constants, not def/class symbols, so _resolve_python_reference cannot resolve them via AST. Fixed both by removing the constant references from source_symbols, keeping only the real function/class symbols already cited alongside them.
10. Ran the full ora suite: 281 passed (279 baseline + 2 new), 0 regressions.

evidence.oracle: none -- this is format_factory's own self-consistent test evidence, not independently cross-checked against an independent OpenRaster reader/writer. Labeled SELF-CONSISTENT per the FF6 execution-recovery directive's GAP-008 rule, not VERIFIED.
evidence.why_9_of_14_moved_and_2_corrected_not_pr: 8 obligations were directly, individually provable by existing or newly-added tests. 1 was a confirmed cross-capability duplicate closed by citation. 2 (930CACD129A5CC40 and its ORA-COMPOSITE-001 duplicate 4EC8C1CC747F7FC6) were corrected from misleading status to accurate partial rather than force-promoted, since a real clause (documented blend-function/Porter-Duff-operator registry) remains genuinely unbuilt and unattempted due to missing verified spec source. 4 remain unaudited, left honestly incomplete rather than rushed.
evidence.anti_fabrication_note: ORA-MASK-001 and ORA-COMPOSITE-001's rendering-adapter obligation were investigated first as genuine-new-capability candidates (following event 139's exact_next_action) but declined: no committed SAL fact enumerates the OpenRaster composite-op inventory or the mask-element XML shape, and building either registry from memory risked fabricating spec content this session does not do. Pivoted to this citation audit instead, which required no such invention.
